title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck's 'Variations sur l'équation des lacets', i.e. his study of the profinite 'loop equations', the circle of ideas that later became the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group. In the surrounding pages:
- Π̂_0 is a profinite (fundamental) group.
- ρ and σ are distinguished elements (loops of order 2 and 3 type).
- N'_ρ and N*_σ are normalizer-type sets.
- Z^!_{ρ,σ} = M^![0] is a group of elements u that preserve the conjugacy classes of ρ and σ up to sign twists.
- ε_2, ε_3 : Z^! → {±1} are characters recording how u acts on these classes.
- S_0Γ^!_{ρ,σ} is a set of triples (u, a, b), with a, b normalizing ρ, σ and u ≡ a ≡ b modulo Π̂_0 up to the ε-twists.
- The page-597 proposition shows that u ↦ (u, a = ε_3(τ')α^{-1}u, b = β^{-1}u) is well defined.

This page states the conclusion of a proposition begun on the previous sheet (588). Take u, u', u'' = u'u with their attached a, a', a''. The following are equivalent:
- (a) a'' = a'a exactly;
- (a') a'' ≡ a'a mod Π̂_0;
- (b) ε_3 = 1 (i.e. a(ρ) = ρ), or σ(a') ≡ ε'_3 a' mod Π̂_0;
- (b') the same with a'(σ) ≡ ε'_3 σ;
- (c), (c') the same with u' in place of a';
- (d) ε_3(u) = 1 or ε_2(u') = ε_3(u').

The chain is proved on p. 588 by working in the finite quotient M/Π̂_0. There the commutator [σ̇, u̇'] is computed in two ways: once as ε'_3 (from the definition of a'), once as ε_2(u') (from (35)).

Corollary. Consider the two subgroups Z^{!!} = ker ε_3 and Z^{!!!} = ker(ε_2ε_3) of Z^!_{ρ,σ} (each of index ≤ 2). Over each of them the set-theoretic section A : Z^! → S_0Γ^!, u ↦ (u, a, b), is multiplicative, i.e. a homomorphic section. Over all of M^![0] it is not.

The next page (599) shows that the projection (u, a, b) ↦ u, on the subgroup S_0^πΓ^!, is a surjective homomorphism with kernel μ = {±1} = {(1, ε, 1)}. So the page computes the 2-cocycle of a central extension of Z^! by μ relative to the section A. Write A(u')A(u) = c(u', u)·A(u'u). Then c(u', u) = −1 exactly when ε_3(u) = −1 and ε_2ε_3(u') = −1. Hence c(u', u) = χ(u')ψ(u), with χ = ε_2ε_3 and ψ = ε_3 viewed additively in F_2. This is the standard bilinear cocycle representing the cup product χ ∪ ψ in H^2(Z^!, Z/2). It therefore splits on ker ψ and on ker χ, which is exactly the corollary.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The equivalence list is deliberately asymmetric: the condition involves ε_3 of the right factor u and ε_2, ε_3 of the left factor u'. That is consistent with a cocycle of product form χ(u')ψ(u).
Z^{!!!} is a subgroup because ε_2ε_3 is a character, so the corollary is sound.
The claim 'not multiplicative over the whole of M^![0]' holds only when both characters are nontrivial on Z^!. This is implicitly assumed.

ideas.what: Criterion for when the canonical lift u ↦ a = ε_3(τ')α^{-1}u into the normalizer N'_ρ is multiplicative, expressed through sign characters ε_2, ε_3 and commutators in M/Π̂_0
ideas.modern_name: computation of a 2-cocycle of a central {±1}-extension relative to a set-theoretic section
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard group cohomology; the specific setting belongs to the GT / loop-equation theory (Drinfeld 1990, Ihara, Lochak–Schneps, etc.)
ideas.where_published: Only the general programme (action of Gal on Teichmüller tower, GT-like group) appears in Esquisse d'un programme and La Longue Marche; this computation does not.

ideas.what: Splitting of the extension S_0Γ^! → Z^! over the index-≤2 subgroups ker ε_3 and ker(ε_2ε_3)
ideas.modern_name: restriction of the cup-product class ε_3 ∪ ε_2ε_3 to the kernels of its factors is trivial

missed.claim: Implicitly, the extension of Z^!_{ρ,σ} by μ = {±1} has class equal to the cup product of the characters ε_2ε_3 and ε_3 in H^2(Z^!, Z/2). Grothendieck records only the splitting over the two kernels and not the cohomological identification. This is a minor technical detail in an unpublished development of the loop equations, not a new result.
missed.quote: est une section multiplicative. Mais elle n'est pas multiplicative au dessus de M^![0] tout entier.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of mild interest to anyone reconstructing Grothendieck's own version of the GT-type group from 'l'équation des lacets'. The sign extension he studies corresponds to a concrete, explicitly describable class.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a technical step, a cocycle and splitting computation, in Grothendieck's private development of the loop equations. It is correct and routine. It is mildly interesting only as documentation of his unpublished GT-type constructions.
transcription_corrections: Line before (60): read 'l'application section ensembliste', not 'application bijective ensembliste'.
After (60): read 'est une section multiplicative', not 'bijection multiplicative'.
'Au dessus des deux α-sous-groupes' should read 'Au dessus des deux sous-groupes'; the 'α' is a misreading of handwriting.
In (59) the first group is written Z^{!!}_{ρ,σ} = M^{!!}[0], with overwritten marks; the transcription's reading is otherwise fine.
Under Z^!_{ρ,σ} in (60) the written 'M^![0]' is attached with an equality sign (Z^!_{ρ,σ} = M^![0]).
